items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: Edgar told me that when Hawk first started playing no one paid attention to him... I always regretted taking that night off. But after that, the public paid more attention to what we had to offer, thanks to Hawk.

ctx.x: The people never applauded when we played except when Freddy and Oscar did attraction numbers. Freddy danced his snake hip routine and played a number on the trumpet and Oscar who could not read a note as big as the piano, could play classical numbers on the guitar and also

did some numbers on a ukelele. Edgar told me that when Hawk first started playing no one paid attention to him. When they played a second number, some people at the bar turned away from their drinks and started to give an ear to what was happening. And by the time they finished a third number, the whole place was digging Hawk and nobody ever was applauded at the Villad'Este the way Coleman Hawkins was. I always regretted taking that night off. But after that, the public paid more attention to what we had to…

And here I would like to mention that there was a second orchestra at the club which played tangos. We each played half-hour sets and therefore the job was not hard. We finished at 2.a.m. every morning, and it was seldom that I went straight home after work. Some mornings, it would be between 9 and 11 o'clock before I got to bed, but I always was on time for the job at 5 p.m. matinee time, and I always felt in good condition.
